label: History
value: Anne attended Queen's Academy.
unit: Anne attended Queen's Academy in a Second Year course alongside her schoolmates, striving hard for top honors like the Avery scholarship and engaging in intense academic competition with Gilbert Blythe. After her schooling, she spent time as a country schoolteacher at Valley Road, where she boarded at 'Wayside' with Miss Janet Sweet, and later taught for three years in Summerside. Over time, her long-standing rivalry with Gilbert turned into deep affection, leading to their eventual engagement to marry. Prior to her marriage, she completed her teaching duties and returned to Green Gables to prepare for her future life with Gilbert.

label: History
value: Anthony Pye attends Avonlea School
unit: Anthony Pye attends Avonlea School and sits at a corner desk. When Anne Shirley begins her term as teacher, Anthony stares at her with a dark, sullen, and hostile expression, firmly believing that girl teachers are no good. He consistently treats her with a scornful air of toleration and refuses to respect her, causing Anne much worry as she tries to win his affection. Eventually, after Anne gives him a whipping, Anthony shifts his attitude and admits that her whipping was as good as a man's, finally earning his respect.

value: Captain Jim is a born storyteller.
unit: A born storyteller with a simple and kindly nature, Captain Jim possesses a vibrant imagination and deep emotional warmth. Despite his soft heart, he retains a fiery intensity when defending his moral principles.

label: History
value: Captain Jim spent much of his youth at sea.
unit: Captain Jim spent much of his youth at sea, enduring numerous wild adventures including a ship fire, Malay pirates, a shipwreck on the Magdalens, and being marooned after a mutiny. Following his seafaring career, he took up the post of lighthouse keeper at Four Winds Point, where he faithfully maintained the light every sunset and sunrise. He rescued an abandoned, starving kitten entangled in a ribbon collar, naming him First Mate and keeping him as a loyal companion. Over time, he meticulously recorded his lifelong memories in a personal journal known as his 'life-book' for his nephew Joe. He formed warm friendships with local residents, including Anne Shirley, Gilbert Blythe, Leslie Moore, and Owen Ford, entertaining them with tea and enthralling true stories. He allowed Owen Ford to use his life-book as the basis for a written novel, which was eventually published under their joint names. Shortly after receiving his printed copy of the book, he passed away peacefully at the lighthouse.

He allowed Owen Ford to use his life-book as the basis for a written novel, which was eventually published under their joint names. Shortly after receiving his printed copy of the book, he passed away peacefully at the lighthouse.

label: Quotes
value: > The boys were fishing for eels over the bridge. Link Drew had caught a whopper—I mean an awful big one—the biggest eel I ever saw. He caught it right at the start and it had been lying in his basket a long time, still as still. I thought it was dead, honest I did. Then old Mrs. Carr drove over the bridge and she called us all young varmints and told us to go home. And we hadn’t said a word to her, father, truly. So when she drove back again, after going to the store, the boys dared me to put Link’s eel in her buggy. I thought it was so dead it couldn’t hurt her and I threw it in. Then the eel came to life on the hill and we heard her scream and saw her jump out. I was awful sorry. That’s all, father.

label: History
value: Carl grew up in Maywater
unit: Carl grew up in Maywater with his siblings before moving to the manse in Glen St. Mary. He became an active member of his family's Good-Conduct Club, through which the children managed their own behavior and discipline. After being dared by older boys, he placed a large eel into Mrs. Carr's buggy under the impression that it was dead, causing her horse to bolt when the eel revived; his father called him into the study for a whipping, but John Meredith ultimately could not bring himself to strike him upon seeing Carl's mother's eyes in his face. To punish himself for perceived cowardice in an earlier incident involving a ghost story, Carl sat on Mr. Pollock's tombstone in the graveyard until midnight during a freezing rainstorm. This exposure caused him to contract severe double pneumonia, bringing him near death before Dr. Blythe and a nurse successfully nursed him through the crisis. Upon his recovery, the local children and Dr. Blythe celebrated his health with a special feast and fireworks in Rainbow Valley.

He became an active member of his family's Good-Conduct Club, through which the children managed their own behavior and discipline. After being dared by older boys, he placed a large eel into Mrs. Carr's buggy under the impression that it was dead, causing her horse to bolt when the eel revived; his father called him into the study for a whipping, but John Meredith ultimately could not bring himself to strike him upon seeing Carl's mother's eyes in his face. To punish himself for perceived cowardice in an earlier incident involving a ghost story, Carl sat on Mr. Pollock's tombstone in the graveyard until midnight during a freezing rainstorm. This exposure caused him to contract severe double pneumonia, bringing him near death before Dr. Blythe and a nurse successfully nursed him through the crisis. Upon his recovery, the local children and Dr. Blythe celebrated his health with a special feast and fireworks in Rainbow Valley.

label: History
value: Charlotta came to live at Echo Lodge.
unit: Charlotta came to live at Echo Lodge to assist Miss Lavendar Lewis with household duties for board and clothes. She frequently entertained herself and Miss Lavendar by blowing a horn or laughing to trigger fairy-like echoes across the river. When Anne Shirley and Diana Barry visited, Charlotta served meals and demonstrated the property's echoes. She worried constantly about Miss Lavendar's loneliness and well-being, confiding her fears to Anne. When Stephen Irving returned to court Miss Lavendar, Charlotta was delighted by his arrival and hoped they would marry so Miss Lavendar would not be left alone. She worked tirelessly alongside Anne and Diana to clean Echo Lodge and prepare for Miss Lavendar's wedding, waking Anne early on the day of the ceremony due to her anxiety about the weather. Following the wedding, Charlotta scheduled her move to Boston alongside Paul Irving to reside with Mr. Stephen Irving and Miss Lavendar.

label: History
value: Miss Cornelia lived in a vibrant green house in Four Winds.
unit: Miss Cornelia lived in a vibrant green house in Four Winds and established herself as a notable local figure known for her fierce devotion to the Presbyterian church and her outspoken dislike of men and Methodists. When Anne Blythe moved to the area as a bride, Miss Cornelia paid her a visit, bringing along baby clothes she was sewing for a struggling neighbor's upcoming child. Over time, she frequently visited the Blythe house to share news, local gossip, and lively debates with Captain Jim Boyd and Dr. Gilbert Blythe. She assisted Leslie Moore with house cleaning prior to Dick Moore's operation and helped support Leslie through financial and practical preparations. Eventually, despite her long-standing reputation as a man-hater, Miss Cornelia surprised the community by marrying Marshall Elliott. Thirteen years after her marriage, she continued to visit Anne and Gilbert at Ingleside to share local news and stay involved in the Glen St. Mary community.

label: History
value: Davy Keith is taken in by Marilla Cuthbert at Green Gables.
unit: Davy Keith and his twin sister Dora are taken in by Marilla Cuthbert at Green Gables. Following the death of his uncle, Richard Keith, a trust fund is created to pay for his maintenance, allowing him to stay permanently at Green Gables. Davy frequently gets into mischief around the farm and school, such as pulling feathers from the white rooster for an Indian headdress, squirming during meals, and ruining cream pies by tumbling onto a pantry table while storing string balls. He shares a fond bond with Anne Shirley, often seeking her approval, asking endless questions, and confessing his bad deeds directly to her.

label: History
value: Diana Barry grew up at Orchard Slope
unit: Diana Barry grew up at Orchard Slope in Avonlea. As a child, she met Anne Shirley in her mother's garden and swore an oath to be her lifelong bosom friend. After an incident involving currant wine, her mother briefly forbade her from playing with Anne, but their friendship was restored after Anne helped treat her sister Minnie May's croup. Diana shared many childhood misadventures with Anne, including jumping onto a spare room bed that turned out to be occupied by her grandaunt, Miss Josephine Barry. She attended Avonlea School alongside Anne and later served as treasurer for the Avonlea Village Improvement Society. Rather than attending Queen's Academy, she remained at home. In adulthood, she married Fred Wright, becoming Diana Wright, and went on to have children, including Fred and Small Anne Cordelia. She actively helped prepare for Anne's wedding to Gilbert Blythe at Green Gables.

label: History
value: Dick Moore grew up in the Glen area.
unit: Dick Moore grew up in the Glen area, spending his summers sailing and his winters clerking in his father's store. Infatuated with Leslie West's good looks and angered by her repeated rejections, he coerced her into marriage by threatening to have his father foreclose the overdue mortgage on her family's farm. They lived together on the West place through the winter, but following Mrs. West's death the next spring, Dick grew tired of settled life and left for Nova Scotia. There, he joined his cousin George Moore on a voyage aboard the vessel Four Sisters bound for Havana. While in Cuba, Dick contracted yellow fever and died shortly after the ship was forced to sail without him. For thirteen years, the locals at Four Winds harbor mistook his cousin George—who suffered severe memory loss and head trauma—for Dick, believing he was alive and impaired.

label: History
value: Dora and Davy are brought to Green Gables by Marilla Cuthbert.
unit: Dora and her twin brother Davy are brought to Green Gables by Marilla Cuthbert after the death of their mother. Unlike her mischievous brother, Dora behaves with quiet propriety upon arrival. She starts attending Avonlea School, where she is temporarily seated with Mirabel Cotton and gets thoroughly frightened by Mirabel's stories about her family's deceased relatives and ghosts. On one occasion, Davy takes her to Mr. Harrison's place to see his parrot, locks her inside a toolhouse on an upturned nail keg, and lies to Marilla and Anne that she is lost, leaving her terrified and cold until Anne rescues her. As she grows up under the care of Marilla and Anne, she continues her studies and helps around Green Gables.

label: History
value: Ellen West resided with Rosemary
unit: Ellen West resided with her younger sister Rosemary in their homestead on the hill near Glen St. Mary. Years earlier, she had been courted by Norman Douglas before his sudden marriage, though she eventually came to regard him almost as a stranger. When the Glen minister, John Meredith, visited their house to borrow a book, Ellen engaged him in a lively conversation about global politics and the potential threat of the German Kaiser. Although she enjoyed Mr. Meredith's company and considered him a fine prospective brother-in-law, she held Rosemary to a past promise that prevented her sister from accepting his marriage proposal. At a silver wedding party hosted by the Pollocks, Ellen re-encountered Norman Douglas and successfully bested him in a spirited argument. Upon returning home late that night, she found Rosemary distressed over having refused Mr. Meredith. Later, Norman Douglas directly confronted Rosemary in Rainbow Valley, persuading her to release Ellen from their old vow so that Ellen and Norman could marry.

label: History
value: Faith grew up at the manse.
unit: Faith grew up at the manse alongside her siblings Jerry, Una, and Carl, enjoying unstructured freedom while missing out on basic domestic training. One Saturday morning, she and her siblings discovered the runaway orphan Mary Vance hiding in Mr. Taylor's old barn and brought her home to feed her. During a house-cleaning endeavor with Una, she accidentally caused a local scandal by shaking house rugs in the old graveyard on Sunday morning. When her cherished pet rooster Adam was slaughtered by Aunt Martha for a visiting minister's dinner, a grief-stricken Faith refused to eat and sought comfort from Rosemary West in Rainbow Valley, forming a close friendship with her. Deeply concerned about her father's parish duties, Faith personally confronted Norman Douglas at his home to ask him to return to church and contribute to the minister's salary, only to be verbally berated and insulted by him. Later, after going to church barefoot due to a lack of intact stockings and facing heavy public criticism, she served a week-long punishment assigned by the Good-Conduct Club by wearing striped stockings to school. To clear her father of any public blame for the incident, she wrote a detailed explanatory letter that was published on the front page of the local newspaper.

label: History
value: Gilbert returned from Alberta
unit: After returning from Alberta, where he had lived for three years due to his father's health, Gilbert re-entered Avonlea school and initiated an intense academic rivalry with Anne Shirley. During his first day back, he teased Anne by pulling her braid and calling her "Carrots," provoking an angry response and years of cold silence from her. Despite this, Gilbert excelled in his studies and pushed to be top of the class alongside Anne. Upon finishing school, he generously gave up his teaching post at the Avonlea school so Anne could stay close to Marilla, leading the two to finally reconcile and become close friends. As they grew older, Gilbert pursued higher studies and confessed his deeper feelings to Anne, though she initially refused his suit. Later, after surviving a life-threatening case of typhoid fever, Gilbert and Anne recognized their true love for each other and eventually married. He became the local doctor in the Glen community, spending nights treating sick patients and caring for their growing family.

label: History
value: In early April, Mr. J. A. Harrison bought Robert Bell's farm.
unit: In early April, Mr. J. A. Harrison bought Robert Bell's farm adjacent to the Cuthbert place in Avonlea and moved there from New Brunswick. He quickly gained a reputation as a crank due to his peculiar domestic habits, such as keeping no fixed meal times and washing all his dishes at once in a rainwater hogshead on rainy Sundays. He got into a heated altercation with Anne Shirley when her Jersey cow strayed into his oats, though he quickly felt ashamed of his temper outburst and accepted her apology after she accidentally sold the cow. Despite his initial gruffness, he developed a warm neighborly friendship with Anne, enjoying her visits, approving of her Avonlea Village Improvement Society efforts, and sharing pipe smoke on his veranda. Though he frequently clashed with Mrs. Rachel Lynde over her outspoken nature and requests for church subscriptions, he eventually settled into a peaceful routine with his wife, Emily, who allowed him to smoke inside near open windows.

Jane eventually became engaged to Mr. Inglis, a wealthy Englishman who made a fortune in mines, and married him in a splendid wedding before setting off on a honeymoon tour of Europe. Following her marriage, she went to live in Winnipeg, remaining sweet, unpretentious, and deeply attached to her old Avonlea friends.

value: John Meredith served as the Presbyterian minister
unit: John Meredith served as the Presbyterian minister at Glen St. Mary, living at the manse with his four young children—Jerry, Faith, Una, and Carl—and his elderly relative, Aunt Martha. Known for his powerful preaching but intense absent-mindedness, he often forgot meetings or practical matters, sparking community gossip and concern over his children's upbringing. Following a confrontation with Mrs. Alec Davis, who offered to take Una, he grappled with his shortcomings as a father and sought comfort in the friendship of Rosemary West. He met Rosemary in Rainbow Valley by a hidden spring and grew deeply attached to her, eventually deciding to ask her to marry him.

unit: John Meredith served as the Presbyterian minister at Glen St. Mary, living at the manse with his four young children—Jerry, Faith, Una, and Carl—and his elderly relative, Aunt Martha. Known for his powerful preaching but intense absent-mindedness, he often forgot meetings or practical matters, sparking community gossip and concern over his children's upbringing. Following a confrontation with Mrs. Alec Davis, who offered to take Una, he grappled with his shortcomings as a father and sought comfort in the friendship of Rosemary West. He met Rosemary in Rainbow Valley by a hidden spring and grew deeply attached to her, eventually deciding to ask her to marry him.

label: History
value: Josie grew up in Avonlea.
unit: Josie grew up in Avonlea as a classmate of Anne Shirley, Diana Barry, Jane Andrews, and Ruby Gillis. During a garden party at Diana's house, she excelled at walking a board fence after daring Jane Andrews to hop on one leg. When Anne belittled the accomplishment, Josie dared Anne to walk the ridgepole of Mr. Barry's kitchen roof, resulting in Anne falling and breaking her ankle. She later visited the injured Anne at Green Gables, though her presence was attributed partly to remorse. Josie attended Queen's Academy alongside her Avonlea peers to pursue her studies, boarding in town and boasting about its superiority over Avonlea. After finishing her initial year at Queen's, she planned to return for further study rather than taking a teaching position.

label: History
value: Lavendar Lewis lives in a stone house.
unit: Miss Lavendar Lewis lives in a secluded stone house bounded by firs and a garden near West Grafton. Having parted from her former fiancé Stephen Irving after a youthful disagreement, she lived out of the public eye for years, attended by her young handmaiden Charlotta the Fourth. Anne Shirley and Diana Barry discover her house while wandering down a secluded lane and are greeted with a warm, festive tea. Anne and Miss Lavendar bond over their mutual love for romance, imagination, and nature, with Miss Lavendar revealing her habit of inventing dream-people to keep herself company. After learning that Stephen Irving's son, Paul, is living in Avonlea, Miss Lavendar eventually invites him to visit Echo Lodge. She quickly forms a fond, special friendship with Paul, sharing games and stories with him. Later, Anne acts as a romantic messenger between Miss Lavendar and Stephen Irving, helping prepare for their eventual reconciliation and wedding.

label: History
value: Leslie grew up as her father's favorite.
unit: Leslie grew up as her father's favorite and enjoyed a happy childhood until a series of tragic events struck her family. At twelve, she witnessed her younger brother Kenneth get killed by a hay wagon, and at fourteen she discovered her father after he hanged himself in their parlor. Despite these traumas, she pursued her education, completed two years of study in one year at Queen's Academy to earn a First Class license, and secured a position at the Glen school to fund future studies at Redmond College. She was later compelled to marry Dick Moore, but after his voyage on the Four Sisters, Captain Jim brought home an impaired man believed to be Dick, whom Leslie spent years faithfully nursing at her home. When Gilbert Blythe advocated for a medical operation in Montreal to restore the man's memory, Leslie borrowed money from Captain Jim to finance it. The operation successfully restored the man's memory, revealing that he was actually Dick's double cousin, George Moore, and that Dick had died of yellow fever years earlier. After assisting George through his initial recovery, Leslie returned home to Four Winds Point freed from her tragic burden. While Susan Baker was away, she stayed with Anne Shirley at the little house of dreams, where Owen Ford courted her.

unit: Jem was born at the little house of dreams by Four Winds Harbor, the eldest child of Anne and Gilbert Blythe, before his family moved to Ingleside in Glen St. Mary. As he grew up, he earned a reputation among his siblings and peers as a good, reliable student, a chieftain at school, and an expert explorer of the natural surroundings. On his eighth birthday, he successfully asked his mother to stop calling him 'Little Jem,' though he maintained a lighthearted feud with Susan Baker over the moniker. Jem spent much of his leisure time playing in Rainbow Valley with his siblings and the children from the Glen manse, often gathering wild mayflowers for his mother or cooking freshly caught trout over a campfire for his friends. On one evening in Rainbow Valley, after Walter spoke dreamily of the Pied Piper, Jem confidently stood up on a hillock and declared that he would gladly follow the Piper round the world.

label: History
value: Marilla Cuthbert and her brother Matthew sent word to orphan authorities seeking a boy.
unit: Marilla Cuthbert and her brother Matthew sent word to orphan authorities seeking a boy to help with farm work, but due to a misunderstanding, Anne Shirley was brought to Green Gables instead. Although Marilla initially intended to send Anne back, she softened upon realizing the mistreatment Anne would face under Mrs. Blewett and decided to keep her. She established strict boundaries for Anne, insisting she be called plain Marilla and instructing her in practical household duties and prayers. When Anne lashed out at Mrs. Lynde for insulting her appearance, Marilla disciplined Anne while privately defending her against Mrs. Lynde's harshness. Later, Marilla also took in her distant relative's orphaned twins, Davy and Dora, giving them small garden plots to teach them responsibility.

She established strict boundaries for Anne, insisting she be called plain Marilla and instructing her in practical household duties and prayers. When Anne lashed out at Mrs. Lynde for insulting her appearance, Marilla disciplined Anne while privately defending her against Mrs. Lynde's harshness. Later, Marilla also took in her distant relative's orphaned twins, Davy and Dora, giving them small garden plots to teach them responsibility.

label: History
value: Marshall Elliott vowed not to cut his hair
unit: Marshall Elliott made a vow during a bitter election that he would not cut his hair or shave his beard until the Liberal party won office. Over the course of fifteen years, he kept his vow, earning a reputation for looking peculiar to strangers while going fishing with Captain Jim. On New Year's Eve, he attended a gathering at Captain Jim's lighthouse, singing Scotch ballads and dancing with Leslie Moore. When the Liberals finally won the election, Marshall went straight to Augustus Palmer's barber shop at midnight and forced the reluctant barber to shave his beard and cut his hair, scaring his housekeeper when he returned home unrecognized. He later met Anne Shirley at the lighthouse clean-shaven, enjoying the joke when she failed to recognize him. Roughly a month after his transformation, he married Miss Cornelia Bryant.

label: History
value: Mary Vance ran away
unit: After running away, Mary Vance was found in an old barn by the Meredith children and brought to live at the manse. She accompanied the manse children to church wearing borrowed clothing, singing lustily in the pew and sticking her tongue out at Mrs. Milgrave when stared at. Refusing to attend school because she felt she had enough education, she stayed at the manse to clean, sweep, patch clothes, and attempt to put things in order. Though she tried to intervene in the household cooking, Aunt Martha kept control of the kitchen. She became a regular companion to the local children in Rainbow Valley, although she refused to play in the graveyard out of fear of ghosts and claimed to have seen hundreds of them. She frequently shared local town gossip, including rumors about Rosemary West, Norman Douglas, and community pranks.

label: History
value: Norman Douglas went about with Ellen West for two years
unit: In his youth, Norman Douglas went about with Ellen West for two years until an unresolved quarrel ended their relationship. Out of spite, he hastily married Hester Reese, whose meek nature he ultimately despised and broke. Following a dispute over a cow deal with a church session member, he stopped attending church for twenty years, though he eventually buried his wife ten years before the arrival of the new minister. When Faith Meredith visited his home to solicit contributions for her father's salary, Norman intimidated her with his fierce blustering; however, after she stood her ground, he promised to attend church starting the first Sunday in November. Keeping his word, he caused a sensation at the service and engaged in lively discussions regarding Mr. Meredith's sermons. Meanwhile, he resumed courting Ellen West, eventually seeking out Rosemary West in Rainbow Valley to request that she release Ellen from a past vow. Upon obtaining Rosemary's consent, he happily prepared for his upcoming marriage to Ellen.

label: History
value: Owen Ford arrived at Four Winds.
unit: Owen Ford arrived at Four Winds for a vacation, intending to gain inspiration for a novel. Upon arriving, he boarded at Leslie Moore's house and was immediately struck by her extraordinary beauty. Anne Shirley introduced him to Captain Jim, whose life-book and stories captivated Owen. Realizing the potential of Captain Jim's experiences and the tale of lost Margaret, Owen began collaborating with Captain Jim, using a lighthouse room as his workshop. Throughout the summer, he threw himself feverishly into writing while joining Anne, Gilbert, Leslie, and Captain Jim on outings. Over the course of the summer, he fell deeply in love with Leslie, whose personality inspired the heroine of his manuscript. After completing his book, he declared his love to Leslie in the little house's garden, receiving her love in return.

Upon arriving, he boarded at Leslie Moore's house and was immediately struck by her extraordinary beauty. Anne Shirley introduced him to Captain Jim, whose life-book and stories captivated Owen. Realizing the potential of Captain Jim's experiences and the tale of lost Margaret, Owen began collaborating with Captain Jim, using a lighthouse room as his workshop. Throughout the summer, he threw himself feverishly into writing while joining Anne, Gilbert, Leslie, and Captain Jim on outings. Over the course of the summer, he fell deeply in love with Leslie, whose personality inspired the heroine of his manuscript. After completing his book, he declared his love to Leslie in the little house's garden, receiving her love in return.

label: History
value: Paul moved to Avonlea
unit: After moving to Avonlea to reside with his grandmother, Paul became a pupil of Anne Shirley at the local schoolhouse. He quickly formed a strong emotional and creative connection with Anne, recognizing her as a kindred spirit who understood his imaginative ideas. During his school years, he invented vivid stories about rock people, fairies, and sunset adventures, confiding them to Anne. He also developed a friendship with Miss Lavendar Lewis, noting her resemblance to his late mother's affectionate demeanor. When his father, Stephen Irving, returned to Avonlea, Paul welcomed him joyfully and helped rekindle the romance between Stephen and Miss Lavendar. As he grew older, Paul matured into a tall youth of six feet, continuing to write poetry and maintaining his warm affection for his former teacher.

value: Philippa Gordon grew up in Bolingbroke.

At her father's insistence, she enrolled at Redmond College in Kingsport, moving into a boardinghouse on Wallace Street. Shortly after arriving, she met Anne Shirley and Priscilla Grant, instantly bonding with them and introducing them into her exclusive social circle. After experiencing dissatisfaction with her initial lodging, she moved into Patty's Place on Spofford Avenue with Anne, Priscilla, and Stella. Throughout her early college years, she enjoyed a wide array of suitors while remaining a steadfast friend to her housemates.

label: History
value: Mr. Phillips served as the schoolmaster at Avonlea School.
unit: Mr. Phillips served as the schoolmaster at Avonlea School. During his tenure, he spent classroom time in the back of the room assisting older pupils like Prissy Andrews with advanced subjects such as Latin and algebra. He maintained order through stern reprimands, once causing Ruby Gillis to cry with his glare after a disruption secretly caused by Gilbert Blythe. After Anne Shirley was late for school, he singled her out for punishment by making her sit with Gilbert Blythe, leading Anne to feel insulted and refuse to attend school for a period. Despite his teaching shortcomings, dedicated students made academic progress in his class, with Anne and Gilbert being promoted to the fifth class under his instruction to study Latin, geometry, French, and algebra. He noted that Anne was particularly struggling with geometry, calling her a dunce at the subject.

label: History
value: Mrs. Rachel Lynde lived in Avonlea
unit: Mrs. Rachel Lynde lived in Avonlea as a long-time neighbor and close friend of Marilla Cuthbert. Upon first meeting Anne Shirley, her blunt remarks about Anne's red hair and freckles provoked an intense outburst of temper from the girl, leading to initial friction before the two made peace. A passionate politician, she traveled to Charlottetown with her husband Thomas and Marilla to attend a political rally featuring the Canadian Premier. She also solicited local subscriptions to buy a carpet for her church vestry room, coming into conflict with Mr. Harrison over his refusal to donate. Following a prolonged illness, her husband Thomas passed away, leaving her in financial difficulties due to an old farm mortgage. Facing the heartbreaking prospect of leaving Avonlea, she gratefully accepted Marilla's invitation to move into Green Gables, taking up residence in the north gable with her own kitchen in the spare room while helping care for the Keith twins.

value: Rilla was sent on an errand from Ingleside by Susan.
unit: Rilla was sent on an errand from Ingleside by Susan to deliver a small basket of early strawberries directly to Mr. Meredith or Aunt Martha. Dressed up in her best hat and clothes, she walked up the manse hill where she encountered Mary Vance. When Mary demanded the basket, Rilla refused to hand it over in accordance with Susan's instructions. Mary then taunted Rilla for being dressed like a doll baby and executed a wild dance around her. After Rilla tried to edge away, Mary grabbed a large dried codfish from a nearby drying rack and chased Rilla down the hill while brandishing it. Terrified, Rilla dropped the basket, causing the strawberries to spill on the road as she fled through the street of the Glen with Mary in pursuit.

value: > It is calm to-night. If there were a wind it would blow your breath away. We get ‘a’ the airts the wind can blow’ up here. This place should be called Four Winds instead of the Harbour.

value: > Una, dear, It isn’t because of you poor little souls that I cannot be your father’s wife. I never thought of such a thing. You are not bad—I never supposed you were. There—there was another reason altogether, Una.

value: > I would never dream of trying to turn your father against you. I would love you all dearly. I don’t want to take your own mother’s place—she must always have that in your hearts. label: History
value: Rosemary was engaged to Martin Crawford at seventeen.
unit: At seventeen, Rosemary was engaged to young Martin Crawford, but he perished at sea when his ship was wrecked on the Magdalens. She and her older sister Ellen continued living together in an old gray house on the hill, remaining quite wealthy and distantly related to Leslie Moore. One evening in Rainbow Valley, she met the Glen minister, John Meredith, by a hidden spring and allowed him to walk her home, finding him far more engaging and eloquent than local gossip suggested. Although she loved John Meredith, she initially could not marry him due to a promise made between her and Ellen. Later, after Norman Douglas confronted her in Rainbow Valley to ask her to release Ellen from her pact, Rosemary agreed so her sister could marry Norman. When Una Meredith traveled up the hill to plead with her to marry her father, Rosemary reassured Una that she would not be an unkind stepmother but a loving friend and sister. She then wrote a note to John Meredith requesting to meet him by the spring in Rainbow Valley.

unit: At seventeen, Rosemary was engaged to young Martin Crawford, but he perished at sea when his ship was wrecked on the Magdalens. She and her older sister Ellen continued living together in an old gray house on the hill, remaining quite wealthy and distantly related to Leslie Moore. One evening in Rainbow Valley, she met the Glen minister, John Meredith, by a hidden spring and allowed him to walk her home, finding him far more engaging and eloquent than local gossip suggested. Although she loved John Meredith, she initially could not marry him due to a promise made between her and Ellen. Later, after Norman Douglas confronted her in Rainbow Valley to ask her to release Ellen from her pact, Rosemary agreed so her sister could marry Norman. When Una Meredith traveled up the hill to plead with her to marry her father, Rosemary reassured Una that she would not be an unkind stepmother but a loving friend and sister. She then wrote a note to John Meredith requesting to meet him by the spring in Rainbow Valley.

label: History
value: Roy meets Anne Shirley in a park.
unit: Roy first meets Anne Shirley in a park during a heavy rainstorm, rescuing her when her umbrella turns inside out. Shortly after, he sends a dozen long-stemmed roses with a poetic rhyme to her residence at Patty's Place and receives permission to call on her. Over the next two years at Redmond College, Roy intensely courts Anne, frequently bringing her orchids, walking her home, and attending campus functions with her. His family later visits Patty's Place, where his sister Dorothy confides how fondly Roy speaks of Anne. Eventually, Roy takes Anne to the harbour pavilion where they first met and proposes marriage in a impeccably crafted speech. However, Anne realizes she does not truly love him and refuses his proposal, leaving Roy heartbroken and bitter as he bids her a final farewell.

unit: Roy first meets Anne Shirley in a park during a heavy rainstorm, rescuing her when her umbrella turns inside out. Shortly after, he sends a dozen long-stemmed roses with a poetic rhyme to her residence at Patty's Place and receives permission to call on her. Over the next two years at Redmond College, Roy intensely courts Anne, frequently bringing her orchids, walking her home, and attending campus functions with her. His family later visits Patty's Place, where his sister Dorothy confides how fondly Roy speaks of Anne. Eventually, Roy takes Anne to the harbour pavilion where they first met and proposes marriage in a impeccably crafted speech. However, Anne realizes she does not truly love him and refuses his proposal, leaving Roy heartbroken and bitter as he bids her a final farewell.

label: History
value: Ruby grew up in Avonlea
unit: Ruby grew up in Avonlea as part of the Gillis family. In her youth, she participated in childhood dramatizations with Anne Shirley, Diana Barry, and Jane Andrews, though she was terrified of pretending to be dead during their play of Elaine. She later attended Queen's Academy, where she was widely considered the handsomest student in her year, and frequently spent her Friday trips home walking with Gilbert Blythe. After earning her license, she taught school at Carmody. Throughout her youth and teaching career, she was noted for her extensive flirtations, receiving romantic attention and proposals from local suitors like Nelson Atkins, Herb Spencer, and Wilbur Blair. During a winter season, she suffered an attack of congestion that led to galloping consumption. Despite her failing health, she remained in denial about her illness and hoped to teach at White Sands in the autumn. She reconnected with Anne Shirley shortly before her passing, expressing a changed perspective on death before dying peacefully in her sleep.

She later attended Queen's Academy, where she was widely considered the handsomest student in her year, and frequently spent her Friday trips home walking with Gilbert Blythe. After earning her license, she taught school at Carmody. Throughout her youth and teaching career, she was noted for her extensive flirtations, receiving romantic attention and proposals from local suitors like Nelson Atkins, Herb Spencer, and Wilbur Blair. During a winter season, she suffered an attack of congestion that led to galloping consumption. Despite her failing health, she remained in denial about her illness and hoped to teach at White Sands in the autumn. She reconnected with Anne Shirley shortly before her passing, expressing a changed perspective on death before dying peacefully in her sleep.

label: History
value: Miss Muriel Stacy served as the schoolteacher in Avonlea
unit: Miss Muriel Stacy served as the schoolteacher in Avonlea, succeeding Mr. Phillips. During her tenure, she took a personal interest in her advanced students, establishing an after-school class to prepare them for the Queen's Academy entrance examination and visiting Marilla Cuthbert to encourage Anne Shirley's participation. She frequently guided her pupils on moral development and good habits, correcting missteps such as Anne's reading of unauthorized novels during class with gentle understanding. Though offered a teaching position in her home district's grade school, Miss Stacy chose to remain in Avonlea out of devotion to her pupils. She coached the Queen's class through their studies, advising them against last-minute cramming prior to exams, and completed her term at the end of June to the deep sadness of her students.

label: History
value: Stella Maynard attended Queen's Academy.
unit: Stella Maynard attended Queen's Academy alongside Anne Shirley and Priscilla Grant, becoming a close chum to both. After completing her third year at Queen's, she worked as a teacher in a back country school for four years. Tired of teaching across nine grades and dealing with unreasonable complaints from parents, she decided to leave teaching and enter the Sophomore year at Redmond College. Disliking the prospect of boarding, she wrote to Anne proposing that she, Anne, and Priscilla rent a furnished house together in Kingsport and have her newly solitary aunt, Aunt Jamesina, serve as their housekeeper.

value: Susan is a household helper.

She derives great enjoyment from discussing neighborhood gossip and morbid subjects such as funerals, yet remains deeply compassionate and fiercely protective of those under her care, especially young Shirley.

label: History
value: Susan Baker was installed as maid-of-all-work at the little house of dreams.
unit: Susan Baker was installed as maid-of-all-work at the little house of dreams to care for Anne Blythe. Following the difficult birth of Shirley, during which Anne was gravely ill, Susan mothered the baby with passionate tenderness, claiming that she gave him life just as much as his mother did. When Dr. Blythe once spanked Shirley, Susan became so indignantly upset that she refused to bake the doctor a pie for weeks. Over time, she moved with the family to Ingleside, establishing herself as the supreme ruler of the household whose domestic authority even Anne rarely questioned. While Dr. and Mrs. Blythe spent three months at a medical congress in Europe, Susan took Shirley to her brother's home to enjoy having him to herself before returning to run the Ingleside home.

unit: Susan Baker was installed as maid-of-all-work at the little house of dreams to care for Anne Blythe. Following the difficult birth of Shirley, during which Anne was gravely ill, Susan mothered the baby with passionate tenderness, claiming that she gave him life just as much as his mother did. When Dr. Blythe once spanked Shirley, Susan became so indignantly upset that she refused to bake the doctor a pie for weeks. Over time, she moved with the family to Ingleside, establishing herself as the supreme ruler of the household whose domestic authority even Anne rarely questioned. While Dr. and Mrs. Blythe spent three months at a medical congress in Europe, Susan took Shirley to her brother's home to enjoy having him to herself before returning to run the Ingleside home.

label: History
value: Una grows up in the manse
unit: Una grows up in the manse at Glen St. Mary as one of minister John Meredith's neglected children. When the runaway waif Mary Vance is discovered hiding, Una takes her in, shares her bed in the attic garret, and comforts her with kindness based on Biblical teachings. Hearing Mary weep over the prospect of returning to an asylum, the shy Una braves her anxiety to visit Miss Cornelia Elliott to ask if she would adopt Mary. When her father suffers deep remorse over his inability to discipline her brother Carl and his broken heart over marital loneliness, Una secretly overhears his agonizing solitude. Motivated by a desperate desire to make him happy, she visits her mother's stored gray silk wedding gown to pray for strength before walking to the house on the hill to plead with Rosemary West to marry her father. Her selfless plea clears up misunderstanding, prompting Rosemary to write a letter accepting the proposal, which Una triumphantly delivers to her father.
